description: Wildfire Risk to Communities is a national set of maps and data that show how wildfire likelihood, intensity and exposure vary across the United States and what that means for homes and communities. Wall-to-wall raster layers give risk to potential structures (the relative risk to a house if one stood on each pixel), burn probability, flame length, exposure type and community wildfire risk reduction zones that indicate where fuel treatment, home hardening or evacuation planning would be most effective; tabular summaries rank every community, tribal area, county and state. The producer is the USDA Forest Service, through Fire and Aviation Management and the Missoula Fire Sciences Laboratory, with Headwaters Economics and Pyrologix, as directed by Congress in 2018. Coverage is all lands in the United States, built from LANDFIRE vegetation and fuels, National Weather Service weather and Census community data of different vintages. GIS files are downloadable by state from the Forest Service Research Data Archive and a spreadsheet from the site, free without registration; no licence is stated, as a federal work. Caveats: values are relative and modelled, inputs differ in date, and the layers do not predict individual fires. Simulation uses: wildfire exposure of fire stations, hospitals and homes, prioritising fire service mitigation and evacuation planning, and climate adaptation scenarios. Related records: HIFLD Open (data-hifld-open) supplies facility locations to overlay.
